sentences.text: I moved seven-day activation at Fernhill from 31 to 44 percent by fixing what happened after people signed up, not the emails.
Whenever a number stalls, the first thing I do is find where people actually drop before I touch anything.
Activation had been flat for two quarters and everyone assumed the welcome emails were weak.
When I looked at the funnel, most people opened the email, clicked, and then stalled on the bank-linking screen.
So I decided the fix was the handoff from email to that screen, and I picked seven-day activation as the number to prove it.
I rebuilt the trigger so the email fired when someone stalled on that step, and I worked with our product designer to cut the screen from three steps to one.
Within a quarter, seven-day activation went from 31 to 44 percent.
That's the kind of problem I'd want to dig into here.
